identification.summary: Storm-1567 is Microsoft's name for the financially motivated operator behind Akira ransomware [S2][S3]. CrowdStrike tracks PUNK SPIDER as the Big Game Hunting adversary, first identified in April 2023, that develops and maintains Akira ransomware and its dedicated leak site [S7]. Microsoft reported that Defender for Endpoint's user containment helped thwart a large-scale remote encryption attempt by Akira actors against an industrial organization in early June 2023 [S2][S3]. Secondary coverage describes Akira as ransomware-as-a-service with double extortion [S9].
identification.firstObserved: CrowdStrike: first identified April 2023 [S7]. Microsoft-reported incident: early June 2023 [S2][S3].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Storm-1567 (financially motivated); CrowdStrike name PUNK SPIDER [S1][S7]. An aggregator also lists GOLD SAHARA as an alias; this is not confirmed by a primary vendor source seen and is not added. Storm-1567 is the actor; 'Akira' is the ransomware family, and CISA's advisory is written about the Akira ransomware variants and their affiliates [S4]. Microsoft's original blog post was not retrieved; Microsoft statements here come from secondary reporting [S2][S3].

attribution.sponsor: Financially motivated criminal group; no state sponsor is stated in the sources gathered [S9].
attribution.confidence: Huntress states analysts have not publicly attributed the group to a specific nation-state or geographic region [S9]. Source-country claims on aggregator sites conflict and are not relied upon.
attribution.basis: Vendor naming by Microsoft and CrowdStrike [S1][S7]; joint CISA/FBI/DC3/HHS/Europol advisory on Akira ransomware activity [S4][S5].

objectives: Financial gain through double extortion: data theft plus encryption, with a dedicated leak site used for pressure [S7][S9]. CISA and partners state Akira had claimed approximately $244.17 million in ransomware proceeds as of late September 2025 [S4][S5].

sectors: Multiple industries; Arctic Wolf describes SonicWall-campaign victims as spanning many industries and sizes [S6]
Critical infrastructure (CISA/FBI warned of imminent threat in Nov 2025 update) [S4][S5]
regions: Reported first spotted targeting Swedish organizations in March 2023 (aggregator, low confidence) [S9]
Otherwise not geographically restricted in sources gathered [S6]
targeting.notes: Arctic Wolf assessed the 2025 SonicWall activity as opportunistic mass exploitation rather than targeted intrusion [S6].

capabilities.summary: Initial access has included compromised VPN credentials, possibly via initial access brokers or brute-forcing VPN endpoints, per the November 2025 advisory as reported [S5]. The update ties intrusions to abuse of SonicWall CVE-2024-40766 [S4][S5]. Arctic Wolf reported SonicWall SSL VPN logins likely using credentials exfiltrated earlier via CVE-2024-40766, including accounts with OTP MFA, with ransomware deployed within as little as 55 minutes and typically under four hours from credential access [S6]. In June 2025 Akira actors began encrypting Nutanix AHV virtual machine disk files [S4][S5]. Earlier, Akira added a Linux encryptor targeting VMware ESXi (reported in 2023) and was reported abusing Cisco VPNs without MFA [S3][S9]. CrowdStrike notes heavy use of legitimate repurposed software and open-source penetration-testing tools [S7]. Microsoft reported attackers used machines not onboarded to Defender for Endpoint, performed reconnaissance and lateral movement, then encrypted remotely using a compromised user account [S2][S3].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated RaaS operator and affiliates tracked as Storm-1567 and PUNK SPIDER [S1][S7].
diamond.capability: VPN credential abuse, SonicWall CVE-2024-40766-linked access, rapid ransomware deployment, ESXi/Linux and Nutanix AHV encryptors, repurposed legitimate and open-source tools [S4][S5][S6][S7].
diamond.infrastructure: Dedicated leak site for extortion [S7]; Arctic Wolf reported new campaign infrastructure through 20 September 2025 [S6]. Specific indicators not collected.
diamond.victim: Cross-sector organizations with internet-facing VPNs, notably SonicWall and Cisco, and virtualized environments; critical infrastructure flagged in 2025 [S3][S4][S6].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal profit motive; no state tasking established in sources gathered [S9].
diamond.technology: Perimeter VPN appliances without strong MFA or patching, unmanaged endpoints outside EDR coverage, and hypervisors (ESXi, Nutanix AHV) [S2][S4][S6].

gaps: Microsoft's original Storm-1567 publication was not retrieved; Microsoft claims come from secondary coverage [S2][S3].
CISA advisory AA24-109A (cisa.gov) and the ic3.gov PDF could not be opened (fetch blocked); advisory claims rely on news summaries and search snippets [S4][S5].
CrowdStrike adversary page content was only seen via search snippets [S7].
Whether SonicWall MFA bypass was achieved by stolen OTP seeds or another method was unexplained by Arctic Wolf at publication [S6].
Alleged Conti lineage and the Megazord variant are reported by secondary sources only and were not independently verified; alias GOLD SAHARA unverified.
Mapping between Microsoft Storm-1567 and affiliates/IABs that perform initial access is not established; cluster boundaries unclear.
No MITRE ATT&CK group ID recorded for this actor.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing VPN gateways, hypervisor clusters (ESXi, Nutanix AHV) and backup servers are key terrain in DoD-adjacent contractor and critical-infrastructure networks [S4][S5][S6]. STEP 2: Fast credential-to-encryption timelines (under four hours, some 55 minutes) compress the defender decision window [S6]. STEP 3: Template is VPN credential access, lateral movement with repurposed tools, exfiltration, hypervisor encryption, leak-site extortion [S5][S6][S7]. STEP 4: MLCOA is opportunistic ransomware against vulnerable VPN-fronted organizations across sectors. MDCOA is simultaneous hypervisor-level encryption at a DIB supplier or critical-infrastructure operator supporting a mission during crisis. Candidate indicators: SSL VPN logins from unusual hosts or after credential exposure, new domain accounts, unmanaged devices on the network, and unexpected disk-file encryption on hypervisors [S2][S4][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor VPN CVE status (e.g., CVE-2024-40766) and credential-reset completion across supported enclaves [S4][S6]. (2) Authorities: DIB and commercial partner networks fall outside DoD-owned DODIN, so response runs through coordination with the owner and law enforcement rather than direct action [S4]. (3) Mission assurance: enforce phishing-resistant MFA, ensure EDR onboarding on all endpoints, and maintain offline backups and hypervisor restoration plans [S2][S4]. (4) Coordination: share indicators through DC3/DIB CS and FBI channels, as DC3 co-authored the advisory update [S4].
